title: Human-in-loop thresholded enactment for KV cache and batching tweaks
creator: Liam O'Connor
description: Implement a human-in-the-loop enactment flow for applying batching and KV-cache configuration recommendations produced by Optimize. The goal is to safely reduce per-token cost while preserving tail latency and output quality. This ticket delivers an enactment controller that enforces thresholded telemetry gates, schedules staged percentage rollouts, surfaces operator approvals when statistical safety windows are breached, and wires up a deterministic rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Operator dashboard shows pending enactments with proposed config diff and estimated cost delta
Canary rollout respects percent schedule (0% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) and advances automatically when telemetry gates pass
If latency or quality regressions exceed thresholds during any stage, rollout pauses and opens a human approval task
Automated rollback can be executed from console or CLI within 15 minutes of a detected regression
All enactments produce an audit record with initial recommendation, telemetry snapshot, and operator decision
tasks: Design enactment controller state machine (stages, time windows, manual override)
Add siteless percent routing knob to runtime request router for staged traffic splitting
Implement telemetry gate evaluator (latency P95/P99, token cost delta, model output eval score)
Console UI: pending enactments page + operator detail view + approve/reject actions
Integrate with rollbacks: API endpoint and console action that reverts to previous active config
Add audit logging and link to existing changehistory stream (s3)
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Simulated dry-run (0%): run recommendation against mirrored traffic for 12h
Stage 1: Canary A (5%): 12h observation window; must pass gates to proceed
Stage 2: Canary B (20%): 24h observation window; automatic advance if gates pass
Stage 3: Ramp (50%): 24h; require passive operator ack if minor anomalies observed
Stage 4: Full (100%): rollout completes, mark recommendation as applied
canary_policy: Latency gate: P99 increase <= 5ms absolute and <= 3% relative over baseline
Throughput gate: no more than 4% drop in sustained QPS on dedicated pools
Cost gate: expected per-token cost reduction >= 7% (projected) and actual reduction not worse than -2% observed
Quality gate: evaluation harness (1000-unit prompt set) must not regress > 0.8% for L2 similarity metrics
Escalation: if any gate fails two consecutive windows, automatically pause and create operator task
observability_checks: Collect baseline window 24h prior to enactment: latency histograms, KV cache hit rate, token counts
During canary windows: sample heavy-tail requests and surface diff heatmap in console
Add synthesized prompts from production prompt-corpus to check semantic drift
Trace-level sampling for any request flagged by anomaly detector for root-cause investigation
rollback_playbook: Immediate automated rollback when P99 latency increase > 15ms or quality regression > 2%
Operator-initiated rollback steps: open console enactment detail -> click Revert -> confirm -> system triggers revert API
Post-rollback: run 1h validation to ensure metrics return to baseline; notify owners and incident channel
For partial rollbacks (e.g., revert to 20% routing): modify router percent key and monitor for 1h before next action

Target pilot customers: three mid-market SaaS customers currently enrolled in cost-savings beta.
